title: Goals That Take Time: Feedback, Cancel and the States a Goal Passes Through

questions.question: Why is an action not just a service with a long timeout?
options: A service cannot carry a goal as large as a trajectory
A service has no timeout at all, so the client would wait for ever
An action is delivered reliably and a service is not
A service that blocks for 90 seconds gives no progress and no way to stop it, and a timeout there means 'I do not know' for the whole time
questions.explanation: A move takes long enough that the caller wants to see how it is going and to be able to stop it. A blocked call offers neither.

questions.question: What does a cancel do to a running goal?
options: Makes it canceled at once, since the client has decided
Makes it aborted, since the goal did not finish
Moves it to canceling: only the server's confirmation, after the arm has actually stopped, makes it canceled
Returns it to accepted, so that it can be started again
questions.explanation: Asking to stop is not stopping. An arm takes time to decelerate, and the goal is canceling until the server says it has.

questions.question: The client cancels in the same moment the arm arrives. What does the goal end as?
options: canceled: the client's request came first and takes priority
aborted: a goal that was both canceled and finished is in conflict
succeeded: the work finished before the cancel took effect, and a client that assumed the cancel worked would be wrong
canceling: it stays there until the client asks again
questions.explanation: The arm arrived before the cancel took effect, so what the robot did was complete the move. The state says what happened, not what was asked.

questions.question: What happens to every call on a goal that has finished?
options: It is applied if it would move the goal to a worse state, such as aborted
Nothing: 0 changed across succeeded, canceled and aborted goals, so a reported result cannot be overwritten
It reopens the goal, so a finished goal can be run again
It raises an error and the server stops
questions.explanation: The test called every method on a succeeded, a canceled and an aborted goal and none changed. A result that can change after it was reported cannot be trusted.

questions.question: Feedback arrives for a goal that was canceled. What should the goal do?
options: Drop it and count it: 2 kept while executing, 3 dropped after
Keep it, so that the client can show the last progress: 5 kept
Restart the goal from that progress: 2 kept, then executing again
Mark the goal aborted, since feedback after a cancel is a fault: 2 kept, then aborted
questions.explanation: Progress describes a goal that is running. For one that is not, showing it would display a move that is no longer happening.

questions.question: A second goal arrives while the first runs. What are the two rules, and what does preempt old do to the first?
options: Reject the new one, or accept it and ask the old one to cancel, which leaves the old one canceling and not yet stopped
Queue the new one behind the old, or run both together, and preempt old runs both
Reject the new one, or accept it and mark the old one canceled at once
Accept the new one and abort the old, or abort both, and preempt old aborts the first
questions.explanation: One arm does one thing. Under preempt old the second goal is accepted while the first is still stopping, so the server must decide whether to wait for the confirmation.
